question: Your team keeps a shared skill named db-migrate in .claude/skills/, and the skill is committed to version control. Priya, one developer on the team, wants a version of this skill that adds extra logging steps for her own debugging habits. Her change must not alter how the skill behaves for her teammates. What should Priya do?

options.text: Copy the skill into ~/.claude/skills/ under the same name, db-migrate, so that her personal copy stands in for the shared one.
options.reason: The guide says personal variants should use different names to avoid affecting teammates; reusing the shared name does not follow that practice.

options.text: Create a personal skill in ~/.claude/skills/ under a different name, such as db-migrate-verbose, that contains her logging steps.
options.reason: The guide describes personal variants created in ~/.claude/skills/ with different names, so Priya gets her variant and teammates are not affected.

options.text: Add her logging steps to the project-level CLAUDE.md file, so that Claude Code loads them in every session together with the shared skill.
options.reason: The project CLAUDE.md is shared with the team and always loaded, so the logging steps would reach every teammate's sessions.

options.text: Edit the shared SKILL.md in .claude/skills/ to add her logging steps, and then commit the change to version control.
options.reason: The project .claude/skills/ directory is shared via version control, so this edit changes the skill for every teammate.
